  CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
  Tuesday, December 19, 2023 - 6:30 P.M.

  425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California 91776

How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

Watch the Meeting Online

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, December 19, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF POLICE DEPARTMENT EMPLOYEE
  ▪ POLICE OFFICER NORI SMITH

  B. CITYWIDE COMMUNICATION SURVEY RESULTS

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of December 5, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  2
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – NOVEMBER 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-2024 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for November 2023.

  D. ADDITIONAL FUNDS FOR ADDITIONAL SCOPE OF WORK FOR THE
  PICKLEBALL COURT PROJECT AT SMITH PARK IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $13,200 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  On July 18, 2023, City Council approved $18,300 towards work at Smith Park.
  This item is requesting additional funds to the existing contract with Taylor
  Tennis Courts, Inc. to include installation of four permanent pickleball courts on
  the east Court and additional pickleball play lines on the west court at Smith
  Park. The revised quote to complete the additional scope of work at Smith Park
  is $31,500. Due to the fact that this is an expansion of resources, with the
  addition of four permanent pickleball courts, this is an eligible expense to Parks
  Development Impact Fee account.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as installation and
  resurfacing of tennis/pickleball courts in an existing City Park does not
  reasonable create a possibility that the work will have any significant affect to
  the environment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  3
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the additional Scope of Work
  as mentioned in Attachment A of the staff report, increase the purchase order
  amount by $13,200, plus a 10% Contingency for a total increase of $14,520,
  from Impact Fund account 124-850-40-97-817, and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the contracts with Taylor Tennis Courts, Inc. accordingly.

  E.  PURCHASE OF FOUR 2024 FORD HYBRID MAVERICK TRUCKS USING
  SOUTH COAST AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT DISTRICT (AQMD) FUNDS
  FOR A TOTAL AMOUNT OF $159,032.88

  The Parks Division is in need of an additional vehicle to help with the daily
  workload between City-owned parks and buildings. One Maverick will be used
  as a general-purpose vehicle for transporting staff, tools, and materials. Two
  Mavericks will be assigned to the Public Works Department inspectors for
  transporting staff and equipment to construction and inspection sites
  throughout the City. One Ford Maverick will become a pool car and general-
  duty vehicle at Public Works. Funds are available in the fiscal year 2023-24
  approved budget under Account Code 124-800-51-99-767.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines, as acquisition and
  replacement of city vehicles is not an activity that creates a reasonable possibility
  of significant impact on the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive formal bidding and authorize the
  Cooperative Purchase Agreement consistent with the piggyback bidding
  requirements pursuant to Municipal Code Section 34.35 and authorize the City
  Manager to approve a purchase order with National Auto Fleet Group in the
  amount not to exceed $159,032.88 from Special Project AQMD budget account
  124-800-51-99-767.

  F.  RESOLUTION NO. 23-71 APPROVING PEDESTRIAN AND BICYCLE SAFETY
  PROGRAM – OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY GRANT IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $55,000 FOR EDUCATION, MATERIAL, AND ILLUMINATED CROSSWALK
  AT THE INTERSECTION OF DEL MAR AVENUE AND LIVE OAK STREET AND
  RELATED BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  4
   The Police Department has received a grant from the Office of Traffic Safety to
  participate in the Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Program for Federal Fiscal Year
  2023-2024. The grant will reimburse the City for personnel overtime costs
  incurred to participate in this campaign and for the purchase of related
  equipment in the sum of $55,000. There is no impact to the general fund with
  the acceptance of the grant.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-71 approving
  and accepting the Office of Traffic Safety contract funding outlined in this Staff
  Report and increasing the revenue budget account #147-3229 by an estimated
  $55,000 to reflect receipt of the grant funds and increasing the Police
  Department expenditure budget by $55,000, in various accounts in Fund 147,
  the Office of Traffic Safety Fund, which will be used for overtime costs and the
  purchase of any related equipment.

  G. AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL, RELATED COMPANIES
  (DEVELOPER), AND THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY HOUSING TRUST RELATED
  TO THE USE OF PERMANENT LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION (PLHA)
  FUNDING FOR THE 405 SOUTH DEL MAR AVENUE PROJECT

  The Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA), on behalf of Los
  Angeles County and its participating cities, has applied for funding for the grant
  program known as the Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) Program
  from the California Department of Housing & Community Development. The
  allocation is based on real estate recording fees, and the City of San Gabriel will
  be allocated $334,526 from the $18 million grant for the period July 1, 2023-
  June 30, 2024 (Year 3). The City has already been allocated $480,191 from
  LACDA for PLHA funding. The City of San Gabriel has the opportunity to utilize
  this funding opportunity toward eligible housing activities as identified in the
  PLHA grant guidelines. As such, staff will be utilizing the $814,777 toward the
  affordable housing project at 405 South Del Mar Avenue. In order to utilize the
  PLHA grant funding for this project, LACDA has requested an agreement
  between the City of San Gabriel, Related Companies (Developer), and the San
  Gabriel Valley Housing Trust (SGVHT).

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  5
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  an agreement between the San Gabriel Valley Housing Trust, Related
  Companies, and the City of San Gabriel for the 5-year PLHA Plan grant period
  subject to City Attorney’s review and approval for legal effect and content.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 23-72 FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAMS: BUDGET AND ALLOCATION

  Each fiscal year, the City of San Gabriel receives an allocation from the Los
  Angeles County Development Authority for the Community Development Block
  Grant Program. For the Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25, the City should expect to
  receive $293,032 (a 2% reduction from the current year’s allocation) to be used
  toward developing viable communities and serving low- and moderate- income
  populations. It is important to note that the final adopted allocations
  distributed by the Los Angeles County Development Authority may vary slightly
  since Congress is finalizing the budget at the time of submission of this staff
  report. The Fiscal Year 2024-25 Community Development Block Grant Program
  and Budget Plan proposes to allocate the funding to the following programs:
  Youth Services Program, Code Enforcement, the Street Improvement Project,
  and a Graffiti Control Program. There is no fiscal impact for the current year
  2023-2024. The Community Development Block Grant funding allocation
  estimate of $293,032 outlined in this report are for the 2024-25 fiscal year and
  represents a 2% decrease (approximately $2,567) from the current year
  allocation.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines, as grant acceptance in
  and of itself, does not have a potential for any adverse impacts to the
  environment. Prior to construction, separate environmental review of individual
  construction projects may be required.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-72 authorizing the allocation of Community
  Development Block Grant funds for FY 2024-25 from Los Angeles County
  Development Authority for activities and projects described above.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  6
   2. Carry over any Community Development Block Grant funds unspent at the
  close of FY 2023-24 and recognize the receipt of FY 2024-25 Community
  Development Block Grant Program funds awarded by Los Angeles County
  Development Authority to the City in the City FY 2024-25 Budget.

  B. AMENDMENT OF AN EXISTING PLANNED DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY
  ZONE, DEVELOPMENT OF AN AGREEMENT AND TENTATIVE TRACT MAP
  / 201-217 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD / PLANNING CASE NOS.
  ZC22-001, AND TMAP22-015 / APPELLANT: EVERARDO GARCIA OF LCRA

  This is a request to amend an existing Planned Development Overlay Zone over
  an existing C-1 (Retail Commercial) zoning designation of the subject site, a
  Development Agreement, and revised Tentative Tract Map No. 73753 to allow
  for the subdivision of air space for residential condominium units within a
  mixed-use development. The property is designated General Commercial in the
  General Plan and zoned Retail Commercial/Planned Development Overlay. The
  applicant will pay a number of fees to the City, including plan check, permits,
  and development impact fees. The City will additionally be in receipt of property
  tax by the sale and improvement of the project site.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  project was reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality
  Act. The City prepared an Initial Study to determine the proposed project’s
  potential impact on the environment. The City has determined that the project
  may have a significant effect on the environment, but by implementing the
  identified mitigation measures, the project’s impacts could be reduced to less than
  significant levels. Ten mitigation measures have been identified to reduce the
  potential impact to a less than significant level.

  The 30-day public review period of the Initial Study / Mitigated Negative
  Declaration was initiated on August 24, 2023 and ended on September 22, 2023.
  A notice regarding the CEQA comment period was posted with the Los Angeles
  County Recorder, published in the San Gabriel Sun newspaper, and distributed to
  the relevant regulatory agencies. Additionally, a notice was mailed to owners and
  occupants within 500-feet of the project site. A total of three comment letters
  were submitted to the City during the public comment period. The comment
  letters and the Lead Agency response to comments received are included in the
  Final Mitigated Negative Declaration.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  7
   The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications,
  or deny the Zone Change/Planned Development Overlay, Development
  Agreement, and Tentative Map applications.

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-73 approving the Mitigated Negative Declaration
  and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program and Planning Case No.
  TMAP22-015 (Tentative Track Map); and

  2. Waive full reading, introduce Ordinance No. 700 by title only, and waive
  future reading; and

  3. Schedule the second reading and adoption of the Ordinance for the next
  regular City Council meeting. The Ordinance would then become effective
  30 days after adoption.

  Alternative Option for Consideration

  Option 1 – Should the City Council determine that the proposed project or any
  part of the proposed project should be denied, the Council should deliberate
  and provide the required findings, direct staff to return with a Resolution for
  the DENIAL of Planning Case Nos. ZC22-001, DA22-001, and TMAP22-015 at
  the regularly-scheduled City Council meeting of January 19, 2024.

  Option 2- The City Council could also discuss the proposed project and suggest
  changes that would allow the project to be approved with modifications.

  C. ORDINANCE NO. 699 ANNEXATION AND PRE-ZONING (AXN23-001,
  GPA23-001, AND ZC23-001) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING /
  5623 NORTH GLADYS AVENUE (ASSESSOR PARCEL NUMBER 5374-027-
  005) / APPLICANT: ALEX ALVAREZ

  This is a request for annexation and pre-zoning for a property located at 5623
  N. Gladys Avenue, on the west side of N. Gladys Avenue, between E. Las Tunas
  Drive and E. Live Oak Street (Assessor Parcel Number 5374-027-005) in Los
  Angeles County. The pre-zoning would change the General Plan land-use
  designation from Low-Density Residential to General Commercial and a Zone
  Change from R-1 (Single-Family Residence) to C-1 (Retail Commercial). Should
  the request be approved by the City Council via adoption of Ordinance No. 699,
  the approval would then be forwarded to the Local Agency Formation
  Commission for the County of Los Angeles for approval. The land-use
  amendment and zone change would become effective upon approval of the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  8
   annexation. The Fiscal Year 2023-24 Adopted Budget includes the cost for
  required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification
  (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments would be exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  under Section 15319 (Annexations of Existing Facilities and Lots for Exempt
  Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines. Annexations to a city or special district of areas
  containing existing facilities public or private structures developed to the density
  allowed by the current zoning or pre-zoning of either the gaining or losing
  governmental agency which is more restrictive, provided, however, that the
  extension of utility services to the existing facilities would a capacity to serve only
  the existing facilities.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed ordinance No. 699.

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 699 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA,  APPROVING  PLANNING  CASE  NOS.  ANX23-001
  (ANNEXATION), GPA23-001 (GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT), AND ZC23-001
  (ZONE CHANGE) FOR THE PROPERTY LOCATED AT 5623 NORTH GLADYS
  AVENUE, SUBJECT TO THE RECOMMENDED CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL.

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next Regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

  Alternative Options for Consideration

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications,
  or deny the Annexation and Pre-Zoning applications.
  If the City Council determines that the proposed applications or any part of the
  applications should be denied, the appropriate motion should be adopted.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  9
   A. AGREEMENT WITH AEF SYSTEMS CONSULTING, INCORPORATED FOR
  ENTERPRISE RESOURCE PLANNING ADVISORY SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $47,970

  The City currently uses Tyler Eden software for financial management needs,
  having utilized the system for over 20 years. Recently, Tyler has communicated
  that support for the Eden system will end beginning in 2027. Consequently, the
  City will need to procure and fully implement a new enterprise resource
  planning system before the specified date through agreement with AEF System
  Consulting. The total cost for the ERP advisory consulting agreement is $47,970.
  The 2023-24 general fund budget included $30,000 for this project. Additional
  budgeted funds will be utilized in the finance department (general fund) to fund
  the remaining $17,970 of this agreement, and no additional appropriations to
  the 2023-24 general fund budget are necessary.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a professional services agreement with AEF Systems Consulting, Inc. for
  ERP advisory services.

  B. AGREEMENT WITH GRIZZLY ENTERTAINMENT FOR A DRONE SHOW FOR
  THE 2024 INDEPENDENCE DAY CELEBRATION IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $45,000

  At the October 3, 2023 City Council Meeting, staff presented an item on special
  events, including options for the 2024 Independence Day Celebration. The
  Council indicated that they would like to have a drone show in place of a
  fireworks show. The total cost for the agreement with Grizzly Entertainment for
  the quoted July 3rd drone show is $45,000. The budget in the general fund for
  this Independence Day event is $50,250. While this does not include staffing
  costs for all departments to work the event, the budget should be enough to
  cover the drone show and entertainment. Depending on the drone count that
  the Council decides on, should additional funds be needed for the
  entertainment and/or auxiliary event costs, staff would ask for additional
  funding at mid-year budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 19, 2023  10
   Recommended Action:

  1. Staff recommends that the Council approve a show with Grizzly
  Entertainment on Wednesday, July 3 for 350-400 drones, at a cost of
  $45,000 and discuss the options for location of the show.

  2. Staff also recommends that the Council authorize the City Manager to sign
  the agreement with Grizzly Entertainment.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT
  The regular City Council meeting of January 2, 2024, has been cancelled. The next
  regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, January 16, 2023 at 6:30 P.M.
  Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be available
  on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

Materials Available for Inspection. You may view agenda items online at

MINUTES OF DECEMBER 19, 2023
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:41 P.M. on Tuesday, December 19, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Wu.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark; Human Resources/Risk
  Management Director Edward Macias, Finance Director
  William Kaholokula, Community Development Director
  Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief Edwin Elizalde, Fire Division
  Chief Christopher Eakman, and Assistant City Clerk
  Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the Agenda Order was
  approved.
  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF POLICE OFFICER NORI SMITH

I  Police Chief Elizalde made the presentation.

  B. CITYWIDE COMMUNICATION SURVEY RESULTS

  Public Information Officer Clara Tsang made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 7  December 19, 2023
   Cheryl Cabot, resident, and Sonia provided comments related to San Gabriel Chamber
  of Commerce municipal membership.

  Cynthia Talavera, resident, provided comments about a recent dog attack in her
  neighborhood.

  Andrew, resident, requested wording changes to the policy regarding military
  equipment which was adopted by the City, and requested that tear gas use not be
  allowed in the City.

I  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Regarding Item 4D, the following provided comments in favor of preference for tennis
  players on one of the courts: Alfred Lin, resident; Ken, resident; Tung Phan, resident;
  Jim Liao, resident; Vicky Hung, resident; Glen Ward, resident; Li-Ken Tang; Bruce Ward,
  resident; Kelly Hung, resident; Wenpingchen, resident; Scott Yeh, resident; Frank Niu,
  resident; Paul Lee, resident; and two anonymous residents. The following provided
  comments or spoke in favor of pickleball players: Dennis Sam, resident; Andre Sam,
  resident; Johnny Lau, resident; Metkeo Orozco, resident; Mitch Borgeson, resident; and
  Sonia Lyn, resident.

  City Manager Lazzaretto provided an update that City staff will be meeting with school
  district officials in relation to securing additional tennis courts for community use.

  Regarding Item 4B, Andrew, resident, questioned staff's professional association and
  conference fees and Council Member conference fees and requested a report to the
  public from those who received the funds.

I  City Manager Lazzaretto clarified that the referenced expenses are itemized in the
  City's budget and that Council Members and Department Directors do an excellent
  job of reporting about those items.
  Regarding Item 4G, Andrew, resident, requested information for the public on the 405
  S. Del Mar Avenue project.

  City Manager Lazzaretto reported that the Community Development Department will
  have a presentation for the community on this project in the early part of 2024.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4G as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of
  December 5, 2023.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved November 21, 2023, and December 4, 2023, Registers
  of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 7  December 19, 2023
   C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - NOVEMBER 2023

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for November
  2023.

  D. ADDITIONAL FUNDS FOR ADDITIONAL SCOPE OF WORK FOR THE
